title: PX-CSI Support for Talos Linux Coming in December
summary: Explore how the upcoming release of Portworx CSI (PX-CSI) will bring Everpure FlashArray and FlashBlade storage to Talos-based Kubernetes environments.
body_markdown:
### Summary


PX-CSI 26.3, included with FlashArray and FlashBlade, adds asynchronous snapshots between FlashArray systems, FlashBlade snapshot restore to a new volume, ActiveCluster stretched pods with realms, and mixed SAN protocols in one cluster. Platform teams get these array controls through standard Kubernetes objects, for containers and KubeVirt VMs.


The upcoming release of Portworx® CSI (PX-CSI), slated for December, will introduce support for[Talos Linux from Sidero Labs](https://www.siderolabs.com/talos-linux) , expanding the range of Kubernetes platforms that can leverage Everpure enterprise storage solutions. For existing Everpure customers, this opens the door to Talos Linux—a minimal, immutable OS with no SSH, shell, or package manager, managed entirely through a declarative API—without giving up the[storage platform they already rely on.](https://blog.everpuredata.com/purely-technical/portworx-helps-mitigate-rising-storage/)


With this release, customers running Talos-based Kubernetes clusters will be able to use Everpure™[FlashArray](https://www.everpuredata.com/products/block-file-object-storage.html) ™ and[FlashBlade](https://www.everpuredata.com/products/unstructured-data-storage.html) ® storage for their persistent storage needs, while benefiting from the familiar Kubernetes-native storage management experience provided by PX-CSI.


## **What’s new with this release?**


PX-CSI will enable Talos-based Kubernetes clusters to consume Everpure storage across multiple protocols and workloads:


- **FlashArray block storage:** Persistent block volumes over iSCSI and NVMe/TCP
- [FlashArray File Services](https://support.everpuredata.com/r/flasharray-file-services/flasharray-file-services) **:** NFS-based persistent storage
- **FlashBlade file storage:** NFS-based persistent storage
- **Kubernetes-native volume management:** Standard CSI operations, including dynamic provisioning, volume attachment, mounting, expansion, and lifecycle management, as applicable to each storage backend


### **Simplified deployment through Portworx Central**


Customers will be able to select Talos Linux as their Kubernetes distribution in[Portworx Central](https://central.portworx.com/landing/login) (login required).


PX-CSI will automatically apply the required Talos-specific deployment configuration, including exempting the Portworx namespace from Talos’s default baseline Pod Security enforcement, simplifying installation and reducing manual configuration.


Talos Linux will also be included in the official[PX-CSI supported platforms matrix](https://docs.portworx.com/portworx-csi/support-matrix) .


### **Integration with Talos system extensions**


Talos Linux follows an immutable operating system model, where host-level utilities are provided through system extensions rather than traditional package installation.


PX-CSI has been adapted to work with this architecture by using container-bundled utilities for general filesystem operations while leveraging Talos system extensions for host-dependent storage operations such as iSCSI and multipath management.


Steve Francis, President, Sidero Labs, notes, “Platform teams choose Talos Linux because they want Kubernetes infrastructure that is secure by default and identical everywhere it runs. With PX-CSI support, Everpure customers no longer have to choose between a declarative secure operating model and the enterprise storage their stateful applications depend on.”


## **What does this mean for customers?**


With Talos Linux support, customers can:


- **Expand**[Kubernetes platform choice](https://blog.everpuredata.com/purely-technical/containers-best-path-forward-post-vmware/) **:** Deploy PX-CSI on immutable Talos-based clusters without changing your existing Everpure storage infrastructure.
- **Maintain a consistent storage experience:** Continue using familiar Kubernetes CSI interfaces and workflows for provisioning and managing persistent volumes.
- **Simplify deployment:** Leverage[Portworx Central](https://central.portworx.com/) for Talos-aware configuration and installation.
- **Embrace immutable Kubernetes infrastructure:** Combine Talos Linux’s security-focused operating model with enterprise storage capabilities from FlashArray and FlashBlade.


## **Availability and requirements**


Talos Linux 1.14 and later support is planned for the December PX-CSI release. Nodes require the appropriate Talos system extensions (iscsi-tools, multipath-tools, nvme-cli, nfs-utils, depending on protocol), which are available through the Talos Image Factory.


An Early Access (EA) program will start this month, giving customers an opportunity to evaluate PX-CSI support for Talos Linux ahead of the planned release in December. Customers interested in participating in the EA program can reach out to their Everpure or Sidero Labs account teams, or emailsales@siderolabs.com if they are not yet customers of Talos Enterprise Linux.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


1. **Does Everpure storage work with Talos Linux Kubernetes clusters?** Yes, planned: PX-CSI support for Talos Linux 1.14 and later arrives in December, with Early Access available now. FlashArray and FlashBlade are supported
2. **How do I use block storage on an immutable Kubernetes OS like Talos?** Talos has no package manager, so host tools such as iSCSI and multipath come from Talos system extensions, while PX-CSI bundles the other utilities in its containers.
3. **Which storage protocols will PX-CSI support on Talos?** NVMe/TCP and iSCSI block on FlashArray, and NFS file on FlashArray and FlashBlade.
4. **How do I install PX-CSI on Talos?** Choose Talos Linux as the Kubernetes distribution in Portworx Central, which applies the Talos-specific configuration, including the Pod Security exemption.
